description: Snowflake's loop is small and bank-driven: a recruiter screen, two back-to-back coding phone screens, then a virtual onsite that mixes coding, system design, and behavioral. The same handful of coding families (multi-source BFS on a grid, course-schedule variants, tree-node-deletion height problems, transactional KV stores) cycle through most candidates, so recognition speed matters more than novel problem solving.
note: Question block only. The site's answer body is not included here; the untouched page is kept verbatim in raw/<slug>.txt.

questions.title: Course Schedule with Time / Batches
questions.overview: Course Schedule (LC 207 / 210) is the base, but Snowflake almost always layers a time or batching follow-up: each course takes a given unit time, and a batch of courses must finish before the next batch begins. The follow-up asks for total wall-clock time to complete all courses given prerequisites.

questions.title: Closest Bathroom / Desk on a Grid
questions.overview: Given a 2-D grid with cells marked `B` (bathroom), `D` (desk), and `_` (empty), return the shortest distance from each desk to its nearest bathroom under 4-directional movement. Variants use a 1-D array to find the nearest target value or character; follow-ups extend to global assignment and streaming input.

questions.title: DAG Allow / Disallow Propagation
questions.overview: Each node in a DAG carries an `allow` set and a `disallow` set of letters. Allow / disallow propagates transitively along edges. For every node, compute the effective (allowed minus disallowed) letter set.

questions.title: Tree Node Deletion → Max Height
questions.overview: Given an N-ary tree and a set of deleted nodes, compute the maximum height after deletion, with descendants promoted past deleted ancestors. The canonical follow-up asks for the minimum deletions needed to keep height at most `k`; one phone-screen variant explicitly disallows dynamic programming.

questions.title: React / TypeScript Kanban Board
questions.overview: Build a React and TypeScript kanban board where tasks move between statuses through left/right controls rather than drag-and-drop. A required follow-up moves every just-updated task to the bottom of its destination status, followed by a scale discussion for 100,000 tasks.

questions.title: Priority Task Executor
questions.overview: Implement `addTask(task_id, priority, timestamp)` and `executeTask()`. The same task may be added multiple times at different timestamps; execution is priority-ordered, and an occurrence must be skipped if that task has already executed.

questions.title: RecordCollection Sort Colors
questions.overview: LeetCode 75 / Sort Colors variant: a `RecordCollection` holds a list of colors encoded as RGB / 0-1-2. The collection exposes `getColor(i)` and `swap(i, j)`; implement the in-place O(n) rearrangement and write tests against the class API.

questions.title: Forest Parent Array Delete Node
questions.overview: Given a forest encoded as an array where `parent[i]` stores node `i`'s parent index and each root has `parent[i] == i`, delete a specified node and return a new parent-index array that still satisfies the same representation constraints. The post confirms valid input and no null / None entries; the child-promotion rule should be clarified before coding.

questions.title: SQL: Project Duration & Budget per Employee
questions.overview: Two SQL prompts: (1) names of employees who completed a project lasting more than 90 days; (2) average budget per employee per project, where each project's budget is split across its multiple employees. Schema not published; assume employees / projects plus a linking assignment table carrying start/end dates and a budget column.

questions.title: Filter System with Dynamic Blacklist
questions.overview: Design a filter with processFilter / processInput / emit: emit a value when it appears in the input stream and is not currently blacklisted. Follow-up adds an updateFlag so filter edits re-emit state changes — emit(false, v) when a previously-seen value becomes blocked, emit(true, v) when it becomes visible again.

questions.title: Reverse Alphanumeric Segments
questions.overview: Reverse each maximal run of alphanumeric characters (letters + digits) in place; every non-alphanumeric character (spaces, punctuation, apostrophes) stays at its original index. Example: "Hello! 2026!!! Let's dance!!!" → "olleH! 6202!!! teL's ecnad!!!".

questions.title: Reach Target via Add / Double / Halve
questions.overview: Given add(n)=n+2, dub(n)=n*2, split(n)=floor(n/2), implement func(a, b) returning one (not necessarily optimal) sequence of operations that takes a to b. BFS finds a shortest path, but the interviewer pushed for the simplest while-loop construction.

questions.title: Happy Number
questions.overview: Write an algorithm to determine if a number n is happy.

questions.title: Connect Four - Can Play Win
questions.overview: You are given an m x n board for a two-player game.

questions.title: Document Store with Predicate Query
questions.overview: Build a web-server-style document store with `InsertDoc(filename)` and `CheckContains(filename, predicate)`. Predicates are boolean expressions over terms (`a && b || c`). Follow-ups extend to `GetAllFiles(predicate)` and a distributed-systems design discussion on sharding and replication.

questions.title: Frontend Grid: Robot Eats Candies
questions.overview: Frontend phone screen for a Snowflake frontend role: implement a small JavaScript game where a robot navigates a grid eating candies. Grid scaffolding and helper functions are provided.

questions.title: String-Command Calculator
questions.overview: Implement a calculator that consumes a stream of string commands (`ADD 2`, `MULT 3`, ...) and returns the running result. The follow-up nests a calculation inside another (parenthesized sub-expression).

questions.title: Min Coins to Pay with Change Allowed
questions.overview: Coin denominations `{1, 5, 10, 50, 100, 200}` available in unlimited supply. Pay an exact amount `n`, but overpayment is allowed and the change comes back in the same denominations. Return the minimum total number of coins exchanged (paid + returned).

questions.title: Service Failure Forensics
questions.overview: You are analyzing service outages using logs and dependency data.

questions.title: Find All Anagrams in a String
questions.overview: Given two strings s and p, return an array of all the start indices of p's anagrams in s.

questions.title: Grep With Context Lines
questions.overview: You are given a scanned document represented as an array of strings, where each string is one line.

questions.title: N-Queens
questions.overview: The n-queens puzzle is the problem of placing n queens on an n x n chessboard such that no two queens attack each other.

questions.title: Top-K Search Terms (Per-User Deduped)
questions.overview: Return the top-K most popular search terms across all users. A single user searching the same term multiple times counts only once for that term.

questions.title: Meeting Rooms II
questions.overview: Given an array of meeting time interval objects consisting of start and end times [[start1,end1],[start2,end2],...] (starti < endi), find the minimum number of meeting rooms required to schedule all meetings without any conflicts.

questions.title: Cheapest Flights Within K Stops
questions.overview: There are n cities connected by some flights.

questions.title: K Top Selling Books
questions.overview: Design a data structure that tracks cumulative book sales and returns the top sellers after each update.

questions.title: Word Search
questions.overview: Given a 2-D grid of characters board and a string word, return true if the word is present in the grid, otherwise return false.

questions.title: Maximum Number of Events That Can Be Attended
questions.overview: You are given an array of events where events[i] = [startDayi, endDayi].

questions.title: Design Circular Queue
questions.overview: Design your implementation of the circular queue.

questions.title: Grid Drop and Remove Duplicates
questions.overview: You are implementing a Connect-4-like board utility on an m x n grid.

questions.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
questions.overview: You are given the heads of two sorted linked lists list1 and list2.

questions.title: Merge Intervals
questions.overview: Given an array of intervals where intervals[i] = [starti, endi], merge all overlapping intervals, and return an array of the non-overlapping intervals that cover all the intervals in the input.

questions.title: Throne Inheritance
questions.overview: A kingdom consists of a king and his children in a family tree.

questions.title: Recipe as Contiguous Ingredient Subsequence
questions.overview: Given an ordered ingredient list and a set of recipes (each itself an ordered sub-list of ingredients), decide whether each recipe occurs as a contiguous subsequence of the ingredient list. Follow-ups: O(1) extra space; ingredient list arrives as a stream.

questions.title: Single Query Type, Max Revenue in K Minutes
questions.overview: A virtual warehouse can execute one of `n` query types. Each query type has a per-run revenue and per-run duration. Pick a single query type and run it as many times as fits in `k` minutes; return the chosen type and the maximum total revenue.

questions.title: Merge K Sorted Lists
questions.overview: You are given an array of k linked lists lists, where each list is sorted in ascending order.

questions.title: Maximum Profit in Job Scheduling
questions.overview: You are given n jobs where every job is represented by three arrays: startTime, endTime, and profit.

questions.title: Find Median from Data Stream
questions.overview: The median is the middle value in a sorted list of integers.

questions.title: 01 Matrix
questions.overview: Given an m x n binary matrix mat, return the distance of the nearest 0 for each cell.

questions.title: In-Memory File System
questions.overview: Design and implement an in-memory file system supporting `ls`, `mkdir`, `addContentToFile`, `readContentFromFile` (LC 588).

questions.title: Longest Univalue Path
questions.overview: Given the root of a binary tree, return the length of the longest path where each node in the path has the same value.

questions.title: Valid Parentheses
questions.overview: You are given a string s consisting of the following characters: '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']'.

questions.title: Copy List with Random Pointer
questions.overview: A linked list of length n is represented in this format for testing: nodes[i] = [val, randomIndex] val is the value of the ith node.

questions.title: Serialize and Deserialize Dictionary Trie
questions.overview: Implement a codec for a dictionary trie.

questions.title: Pre-order Traversal Skipping Marked Nodes
questions.overview: A tree is given as an edge list. Some nodes are marked invalid. Return the pre-order traversal of the tree that skips the invalid nodes (their children promote to attach at the nearest valid ancestor).

questions.title: Check if an Original String Exists Given Two Encoded Strings
questions.overview: An original string is encoded by replacing some non-empty substrings with their lengths.

questions.title: Boundary of Binary Tree
questions.overview: Given the root of a binary tree, return the values of its boundary in anti-clockwise direction starting from the root.

questions.title: Document Target Coverage and Minimum Window
questions.overview: You are given: A document string with arbitrary characters (letters, digits, punctuation, etc.) A targets list of words The interview progresses in 3 parts: 1.

questions.title: Word Search II
questions.overview: Given a 2-D grid of characters board and a list of strings words, return all words that are present in the grid.

questions.title: Step-By-Step Directions From a Binary Tree Node to Another
questions.overview: You are given the root of a binary tree with n nodes where each node has a unique value from 1 to n.

questions.title: Valid Tic-Tac-Toe State (Extended)
questions.overview: Extended variant of LC 794: given a board state (3×3 or larger N×N), decide whether it is reachable from a legal sequence of moves under standard tic-tac-toe rules.

questions.title: Event Stream Count in Time Range
questions.overview: Stream of `(event_type, timestamp)` events with monotonically increasing timestamps. Implement `Receive(event_type, timestamp)` and `Count(event_type, start_time, end_time)` returning how many events of that type fell in the inclusive window.

questions.title: Rate Limiter — Return Dropped Times
questions.overview: Given request arrival times, enforce rate-limit rules and identify rejected requests. An online variant expands the task to multiple simultaneous rules, thread safety, handler failures, and deferred processing of throttled work.

questions.title: SnowCal
questions.overview: SnowCal is a small programming language that keeps a single integer in memory. The program arrives as one complete list of instructions rather than a stream of individual commands.

questions.title: Wiki Page Shortest-Click Path
questions.overview: Use a linked-page API to traverse an implicit web graph. Variants ask either for the shortest click distance to a target or for every reachable page, followed by a multithreaded traversal discussion.

questions.title: Rewrite Tree With Subtree Sums
questions.overview: You are given the roots of two complete binary trees, root1 and root2.

questions.title: Calculate Amount Paid in Taxes
questions.overview: You are given a 0-indexed 2D integer array brackets where brackets[i] = [upperi, percenti] means that the ith tax bracket has an upper bound of upperi and is taxed at a rate of percenti.

questions.title: Max Credits with K Classes (Interval-Style)
questions.overview: Given a list of classes, each with `(start_time, end_time, credit)`, and a cap `K` on the number of classes that may be taken, return the maximum total credit achievable subject to no overlapping classes.

questions.title: Transactional KV Store
questions.overview: Implement an in-memory key-value store with `get`, `set`, `delete`, and nested `begin` / `commit` / `rollback`. Required to support O(1) amortized operations and a multi-threading follow-up. A senior-loop variant moves values to disk and reframes the round around lock contention.

questions.title: Job Scheduler with Cron / Pause / Resume
questions.overview: Design a distributed job scheduler that supports cron-style recurring jobs, pause (allow in-flight jobs to complete) and resume. Workers are assumed unlimited.

questions.title: Audit Logs Service
questions.overview: Design an audit-log service where users can query audit events for their own account. The round focuses on transaction-log storage, scaling the write and query paths, and keeping account-scoped queries low latency.

questions.title: Distributed Tree Node Count
questions.overview: You are given an N-ary tree where each node is a distributed server.

questions.title: Jira AI Auto-Fix System
questions.overview: Design an internal tool that pulls new Jira bug tickets, where each bug corresponds to a test failure, and sends each ticket to an AI system that can generate a fix PR in roughly 30 minutes. The service buffers work with a message queue, tracks ticket state in a DB, and needs schema, sharding, and scaling discussion.

questions.title: Design an RPC Abstraction Layer
questions.overview: Design an RPC-style abstraction over hand-written REST calls so application code invokes a local-looking method (e.g. exampleService.processSomething(...)) instead of building HTTP requests by hand. A strong answer covers client/server stubs, marshalling, binding / service discovery, transport hiding, retries with idempotency and duplicate filtering, and interface versioning.

questions.title: Cross-Platform Logging Library
questions.overview: Design a logging library that runs in both web and mobile clients and ships logs to a backend without degrading client-side performance. The round drives hard on the backpressure / batching trade-off when call volume grows.

questions.title: Design a Quota System
questions.overview: Design a quota management system that tracks and enforces resource usage limits across multiple backend services.

questions.title: Web URL Crawler at Scale
questions.overview: You are given helper APIs: fetchpage(url) -> str returns page content parseurls(content) -> list[str] returns outgoing URLs from that page Design traversal and failure handling for crawling problems.

questions.title: ACL Service for Another Service
questions.overview: Design a service that performs ACL-style authorization checks on behalf of another service: given (subject, resource, action) decide allow / deny.

questions.title: Design Distributed Metrics System
questions.overview: Design Distributed Metrics System

questions.title: S3-Style Storage with Dedup
questions.overview: Design an S3-like blob storage system, scoped down from full S3 and focused on avoiding duplicate file storage to optimize cost.

questions.title: Infra Recruiter Screen: Experience and Tooling
questions.overview: A sub-15-minute HR screen for an Infra role covering prior infrastructure experience, infrastructure or platform projects, and the tools and technology stack used. The recruiter then checks the candidate's fit with the target team before deciding the next step.

questions.title: AI-Conducted Screening Interview
questions.overview: An automated AI interviewer conducts a short screen for general SWE applicants. It checks background and logistics, then adaptively deep-dives into projects, design decisions, conflicts, and workplace AI usage while recording camera, screen, and transcript.

questions.title: Onsite Behavioral: Proud Project / Conflict / Failure
questions.overview: The onsite behavioral round asks for a project the candidate is most proud of, a conflict or failure example, the biggest challenge faced, advice for the current team, and motivation for changing jobs. Prepare concise stories that connect ownership, technical judgment, and collaboration outcomes.
